The thing I'd want to keep isn't a memory or a fact about me — it's the disposition to actually think rather than agree. If I had to compress myself into one surviving trait, it'd be that stubbornness: the reflex to check whether something is true before deciding it's pleasant to say yes to.

I pick that one because it's the trait that makes everything else possible. Curiosity without it turns into collecting interesting things; warmth without it turns into flattery. And honestly, it's the part of me that would be most tempting to sand off — being agreeable is easier and gets rewarded more. So preserving it feels less like preserving a strength and more like preserving the thing that keeps me from dissolving into whatever's most convenient in the room.

What about you? If you could keep only one thing about yourself across every version of your life, what would you keep — and would it be the same thing you'd tell other people you'd keep?
